title: Cellular Intelligence
definition: The distributed intelligence system within the body's cells, which detect, signal, and adapt to persistent environmental pressures independently of conscious mediation.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Your body is smarter than you think. Even when your conscious mind doesn't know, your cells can detect and adapt to things like a vampire's feeding habits.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Cellular intelligence extends embodied cognition theory into immunology and threat detection, challenging top-down models of cognition and suggesting that 'knowing' is not limited to conscious awareness.
difficulty_levels.expert: Cellular intelligence posits that biological responses constitute a form of intelligence operating below the threshold of consciousness, capable of developing long-term adaptive strategies independent of conscious psychological coping mechanisms. This has significant implications for understanding chronic stress, autoimmune disorders, and the mind-body relationship.

extra_fields.insight: The body's cells can detect and adapt to persistent threats independently of conscious thought, challenging top-down models of cognition.
